podcast.title: Censorship and Delayed Release
podcast.body: The album, released in 1968, faced substantial censorship problems concerning both its original cover art and certain songs. These issues led to a five-month delay in its release, and it ultimately came out with a completely blank white cover featuring only the band's name and the album title, a direct consequence of the censorship. "el vegan zwankett que es el grandísimo album que saldría en 1968 tenía problemas de censura de la portada, tenía un problema de censura con las canciones... al final con cinco meses de retraso con una portada que como fue censurada quedó completamente en blanco solo con el nombre de los Rolling Stones y con el título del disco salía el grandísimo vegan zwankett."

podcast.title: Critical and Commercial Triumph
podcast.body: Despite the initial challenges with production and censorship, *Beggar's Banquet* was met with overwhelming critical acclaim and promptly returned The Rolling Stones to the number one position, solidifying their status as "the greatest" band once more. "tenía unas enormes críticas volvían o traezan número uno volvían a ser los más grandes."

podcast.title: Swift Production
podcast.body: Following the success of the "Jumpin' Jack Flash" single, The Rolling Stones quickly entered the recording studio. Within just a few months, they completed this album, which would go on to be considered by many as potentially the best album of their career. "Se cerraron en el estudio de grabación y en menú unas pocos meses se acababan posiblemente el mejor disco de la carrera de los Rolling Stones."

podcast.title: White Album Coincidence
podcast.body: The release of *Beggar's Banquet* with a minimalist white cover, forced upon the band by censorship, coincidentally occurred at the same time as The Beatles' self-titled "White Album." This led to an unexpected parallel between the two major bands' album aesthetics, though The Rolling Stones' choice was involuntary. "volvía a tener problemas porque coincidía con el lanzamiento del guay de Albueno de los Beatles y ellos acaban de un album en blanco no porque quisieran que fuese blanco sino porque su portada había sido completamente censurada."
